lessons.title: Ask an analytical question
lessons.body:
### Define the grain
The grain describes what one row represents. An imported sales row might represent a product entry rather than a customer order. Know this before counting rows.

### Build the query in layers
Filter relevant inputs, group by the dimensions you need, calculate measures, and order the output. CTEs can make intermediate steps readable.

### Use the lab
Import CSV, JSON, or Parquet. The schema explorer shows the table and column names available to your queries.

lessons.title: Window functions preserve rows
lessons.body:
### Aggregation versus a window
GROUP BY reduces rows into groups. A window function computes a value over related rows while retaining individual rows.

```sql
SELECT category, product, amount,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
         PARTITION BY category ORDER BY amount DESC, product
       ) AS position
FROM exercise_sales;
```

Use a deterministic tie-breaker when choosing a single row. RANK can assign the same rank to tied values; ROW_NUMBER assigns distinct numbers.

exercises.title: Find the top product per category
exercises.prompt: Return the highest-priced product in each category from exercise_sales. When amounts tie, choose the product that sorts first by name. Output category, product, amount ordered by category.
hints: Use ROW_NUMBER with PARTITION BY category.
Filter the numbered rows in an outer query or CTE.
